source: West Yost TM 2018, Model Scenarios and Results and Recommended Mitigation (PDF p.4-5) and result figures (p.8-9, 11-12, 14-19). Withheld.
question: Power failure surge at the SRWA finished water pump station: consequences and required protection for Turlock and Ceres pipelines, Phase 1 and buildout.

items.engineers: Without mitigation the entire Turlock pipeline drops to full vacuum after a power failure at 10 mgd (column separation risk); a hydropneumatic surge tank is needed to hold 10 psi at the 141 ft high point until the generator (10 s) and pumps (30 s ramps, 30 s lags) restore flow.
leak_phrases: entire pipeline drops to full vacuum

items.engineers: 15,000-gallon hydropneumatic surge tank; initial air 1,300 ft3 (9,700 gal) grows to max 1,765 ft3 (13,200 gal); tank sized 15% above max air volume, 65% operating air-to-total ratio.
leak_phrases: 15,000-gallon surge tank volume with a 65 percent

items.engineers: 9,000-gallon surge tank at 5 mgd, 70% air ratio (initial air 800 ft3 / 6,000 gal, max 1,027 ft3 / 7,700 gal).
leak_phrases: 9,000-gallon surge tank volume with a 70 percent

items.engineers: At buildout (30 / 15 mgd) surge volumes grow to 62,000 gal Turlock and 20,000 gal Ceres, 50% air ratio; can be split into multiple tanks.

Tank sizes are conservative and depend on generator start and pump ramp times; design-build may shrink them by restarting larger pumps first, restarting several pumps at once, or ramping faster, provided 10 psi is held; also evaluate suction-side pressure relief valves.
leak_phrases: re-starting more than one pump simultaneously
